To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) scFv‐ETAs can specifically bind to their receptor targets; (2) the binding of scFv‐eta to its receptor can lead to inhibition of tumor cell growth in vitro; and (3) the scFv‐etAs can lead to inhibition or retardation of tumor growth in vivo.
(1) The scFv(25)‐ETA protein specifically binds the EGF receptors and inhibits the growth of EGF receptor overexpressing tumor cells.
The anti‐tumor effects of scFv‐ETAs directed against the erbB‐ 2 receptor are enhanced when combined with the EGF receptor‐directed scFv(2 25)‐ETA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel therapeutic agents for the treatment of erbB‐over‐expressing tumors.
the use of recombinant DNA techniques to generate single‐chain antibody‐toxin fusion proteins which specifically recognize and kill tumor cells.
the design of novel recombinant proteins with the potential to treat human tumors which over‐express the EGF receptor or the erbB‐ 2 receptor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the scFv‐ETAs are effective in the treatment of established human tumors in athymic nude mouse models.
the scFv‐ETAs are promising agents in tumor therapy.
the use of scFv‐toxins in cancer therapy is a promising strategy which warrants further development and testing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new strategy for the targeted therapy of cancer, which involves the generation of single‐chain antibody toxin fusion proteins which specifically target the erbB‐related receptor tyrosine kinase family members and which can inhibit tumor cell growth.
scFv‐toxins are very promising for the treatment of erbB‐over‐expressing tumors.
scFv(2225)‐ETA is more potent in inhibiting the growth of EGF receptor overexpressing tumors than the parental antibody 22S.
The main takeaway from our work is that
scFv‐toxins directed against the EGF receptor and the erbB‐ 2 receptor can be used to inhibit the growth of tumor cells expressing both receptors.
the combination of scFv‐ETAs specific for the erbB‐ 2 and EGF receptor is a promising approach to treat tumors which express both receptor proteins.
the EGF receptor‐directed toxin scFv(222)‐ETA has a significant anti‐tumor effect on A431 xenografts.
